title: The epidemic that sails past the line
hook: Herd immunity at R0 = 3 needs 67% immune. Does the epidemic stop when it gets there?

knows: R0 is the average number infected by one case in a fully susceptible population
doesNotKnow: that an unchecked epidemic keeps going after the peak
that the final share infected ends well beyond the threshold

misconception: Once the herd-immunity threshold is passed, the epidemic stops there.
objective: The learner can explain that the threshold marks where cases start to fall (the peak), not where infection stops; people sick at the peak keep infecting others, so with R0 = 3 about 94% are eventually infected in a simple model, not 67%.

claims.text: In the simple well-mixed SIR model, the final share ever infected z solves z = 1 - e^(-R0 z); for R0 = 3 that is about 94% (z = 0.9405), above the 67% threshold 1 - 1/3.
claims.source: Kermack W.O. & McKendrick A.G. (1927) Proc. R. Soc. A 115:700-721; Diekmann, Heesterbeek & Britton (2013) Mathematical Tools for Understanding Infectious Disease Dynamics. Fixed-point iteration in node gives 0.9405 (artifacts/scratch/w2life/check.mjs).

claims.text: On the stage (R0 = 3, 5 days infectious, 0.1% infected on day 0): the peak is on day 19, when 65% have had it and 30% are sick; by day 100, 94% have been infected. For R0 = 2 and 4 the final shares are 80% and 98%.
claims.source: Deterministic SIR, Euler step 0.01 day, replicated in artifacts/scratch/w2life/sir.mjs: peak day 19.2 (rounded to 19), ever infected 0.6545 at day 19, 0.9407 at day 100; R0 2 gives 0.7972, R0 4 gives 0.9803. No random seed.

claims.text: In the SIR model, new cases peak exactly when the susceptible share falls to 1/R0, that is when the herd-immunity threshold is crossed; after that each case infects fewer than one other, but those already sick still infect more.
claims.source: dI/dt = (beta S - gamma) I is zero when S = gamma/beta = 1/R0 (Diekmann et al. 2013).

claims.text: The model is a made-up disease with random mixing, lasting immunity and no behaviour change, vaccines or treatment; real epidemics differ.
claims.source: Model choice in Demo.tsx; stated on the stage before the prediction and in the reveal.

recall.question: In a simple well-mixed model with no interventions, what happens to new infections right after the herd-immunity threshold is crossed?
options: They start to fall, but many more people still get infected
They keep rising as fast as before
They start to fall and no one else is infected
recall.why: The threshold is the peak: each case now infects fewer than one, but the many people sick at that moment still pass it on, so the total overshoots the threshold.
